title: dong, deh and kan
pattern: request + dong (come on) · decision + deh (OK then) · Kan … (you know) · …, kan? (right?)
explanation: dong adds a friendly push to a request, or an 'obviously': Ayo dong! (Oh, come on!), Cerita dong (Go on, tell me), Iya dong (Of course!). deh marks giving in or making up your mind: Ya udah, deh (OK then, fine), Aku ikut deh (OK, I'll come). It also sweetens a suggestion: Coba deh (Go on, try it). kan, short for bukan, looks for agreement: at the end it's 'right?' (Besok libur, kan?), and at the start it's 'you know' or 'after all' (Kan sudah saya bilang, I told you, didn't I).
natural: All three belong to relaxed talk with friends, a partner and family your own age. kan is the most widely usable: a soft …, kan? to check a fact is fine with almost anyone.
stiff: dong in a request to someone older or senior sounds pushy, even rude: ask Bisa tolong …? instead. A sharp Kan sudah saya bilang! is a told-you-so, and a sighed deh can sound like you're giving in reluctantly.

examples.english: Go on, tell me, how was the holiday?

gap.why: dong gives a request a friendly push: 'go on, tell me'.

examples.registerNotes: Casual, to a friend just back from a trip. Gimana is the spoken bagaimana.

gap.why: deh marks a decision you've just come round to: 'OK then'.

examples.registerNotes: Casual, after a friend has talked you into something. Politely: Baik, saya ikut.

examples.english: The shop's closed tomorrow, isn't it?

gap.note: Bukan, the full form kan comes from, is right too, and a little more careful.
gap.why: kan at the end checks something you think is true: 'isn't it?'.

examples.indonesian: Kan sudah saya bilang, hari Minggu pasti ramai.
examples.english: I told you, didn't I? It's always packed on Sundays.

gap.after: sudah saya bilang, hari Minggu pasti ramai.
gap.why: kan at the start means 'you know, as I said'.

examples.pitfallNote: With a laugh this is teasing; said sharply it's a told-you-so, so think twice before using it on someone older.
